hints: For each bottom row, record the height of the consecutive empty run ending at each column.
A rectangle ending at this row corresponds to an interval in the height histogram.
Use a monotone stack to group intervals by their minimum height, then aggregate their width and height contributions with difference arrays.
analogy: Each histogram bar is a ceiling: an interval can hold every building height up to its lowest ceiling.
example: In a completely empty 2 by 3 grid there are six 1 by 1 placements, four 1 by 2 placements, and two 2 by 2 placements.
algorithm: For each row update histogram heights and use a monotone stack with a consistent tie rule to assign every column interval to one minimum bar. If its left and right choices are L and R, the number of assigned intervals of each width is a triangular (piecewise linear) function of width; all heights from 1 through the bar height are valid. Add those linear width ranges to a two-dimensional difference structure over height and width, then prefix-sum to obtain every size count.
correctness: Every empty rectangle has one bottom row and one histogram interval. The tie rule assigns that interval exactly once, and its minimum height is precisely the largest allowed building height.
